subject: Equinox renewal + expansion — bridge credit proposal & term sculpting
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Maria Santos <maria.santos@equinoxai.com>, Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@equinoxai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Equinox renewal + expansion — bridge credit proposal & term sculpting

Hi Maria / Carlos,

Thanks again for taking the call last week. Per our conversation: Equinox is planning to renew the current commitment and add ~35% additional capacity for Q3–Q4 workloads (burst for model retraining and embeddings). Procurement asked us to hold pricing flat for 12 months and to avoid large up-front changes to the MRR cadence.

Attached is a clean-first draft of the amendment that does two things we discussed:
- Adds a 35% capacity uplift to start on 2028-07-01 (phased across two tranches).
- Applies a temporary bridge credit to offset one quarter of the incremental unit cost while usage ramps.

High-level trade-offs we propose: 1) a 12-month price hold on the base SKU for their current commit, 2) a tranche-based uplift with a bridge credit (one quarter of uplift billed at 50% to smooth procurement optics), and 3) a burst pool for on-demand spikes (metered). This preserves your SLAs while delivering predictable unit economics for Equinox.

If this looks directionally right I can loop in finance/legal and ship a redlined amendment (DocuSign link included once we align). Can we schedule a 30-min procurement review on Thursday?

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: EQX_Amendment_draft_v3.pdf (proposal)
Attachment: usage-forecast_Q2-Q4.xlsx (customer forecast)

From: Maria Santos <maria.santos@equinoxai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@equinoxai.com>
Cc: procurement@equinoxai.com
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Equinox renewal + expansion — bridge credit proposal & term sculpting

Jordan — thanks for the draft. A few notes from procurement and infra: 

- Procurement: a 12-month price hold on the existing committed units is non-negotiable. We will accept a phased uplift only if the first tranche is <20% and the bridge credit covers at least 50% of delta for Q3. We need standard language around audit logs, data residency, and a clear termination right if usage drops below the committed baseline.
- Infra: the burst pool looks fine but we need a clear cap and pre-warm SLA; also ask that model inference latency SLOs remain unchanged for the expanded capacity.

Carlos and I will be on the call Thursday at 10am PT. Please come prepared with the burst pool cap and the exact credit math in the amendment. Also upload a single PDF that contains redlines — our procurement team will circulate internally.

—Maria
Maria Santos
Head of Procurement, Equinox AI
maria.santos@equinoxai.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Equinox renewal + expansion — procurement asks (internal)

Internal thread — quick ask before the call: procurement wants the first tranche <20% and bridge credit >=50% of the uplift delta for Q3. Also require termination language if usage drops under baseline. Infra wants a capped burst pool and pre-warm SLA.

Proposed compromise (my thinking):
1) Tranche 1: 18% uplift starting 2028-07-01, Tranche 2: remaining uplift 30 days later.
2) Bridge credit: credit 50% of the per-token uplift for Q3 only (applied as a dollar credit on the invoice).
3) Burst pool: metered pool capped at 1.8x baseline for on-demand spikes; pre-warm window (30 min) with guaranteed capacity provisioning SLA for critical endpoints.
4) Termination: 60-day right to unwind uplift if 3-month trailing usage falls below 85% of committed baseline.

Ben — can you confirm finance is comfortable with a one-quarter 50% credit and the invoicing treatment? Laura — legal redline on termination language acceptable? I can present live on the call.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Equinox renewal + expansion — procurement asks (internal)

Jordan — finance is okay with the one-quarter 50% credit as long as we: (a) cap the aggregate credit exposure to a fixed dollar amount tied to the forecast (we should pull the forecast to set the cap), and (b) require the uplift to be invoiced monthly so credits can be applied against each invoice rather than as a lump retro credit.

I'll calculate two cap options by EOD for the call: conservative cap (based on Q3 75th percentile forecast) and upside cap (95th percentile).

Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Finance, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Maria Santos <maria.santos@equinoxai.com>, Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@equinoxai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Equinox renewal + expansion — bridge credit proposal & term sculpting

Maria / Carlos — thanks for the feedback and for joining this morning. To keep the thread tidy I summarized the mutually agreed bullets below and attached the redlined amendment for procurement review. Quoted the call decisions and next steps.

Call decisions (agreed):
- Tranche structure: 18% uplift (2028-07-01), remainder 30 days later.
- Bridge credit: 50% of the delta unit cost applied to uplifted units for Q3 only.
- Credit cap: fixed at $75,000 (conservative cap; Ben provided brackets during the call).
- Burst pool: metered pool capped at 1.8x baseline; pre-warm provisioning SLA (30-min) for named critical endpoints.
- Termination / unwind: 60-day unwind if 3-mo trailing usage <85% of committed baseline.

Next steps:
1) Redwood to upload a single PDF redline (attached) and create a DocuSign envelope with the amendment — I will include procurement@equinoxai.com on the signing order.
2) Ben to finalize cap math and confirm invoicing cadence (monthly invoice application of credits).
3) Laura/legal to review termination language and any audit log/data residency clauses.

I've attached: EQX_Amendment_draft_v3.pdf (redlined), usage-forecast_Q2-Q4.xlsx (source numbers). DocuSign link will follow when we create the envelope.

If that matches your understanding, I'll send the DocuSign link by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: EQX_Amendment_draft_v3.pdf (redlined amendment)
Attachment: usage-forecast_Q2-Q4.xlsx

From: Maria Santos <maria.santos@equinoxai.com>

Subject: Re: Equinox renewal + expansion — bridge credit proposal & term sculpting

Jordan — this matches. Procurement will review the redline and aim to turn the DocuSign back within 48 hours pending legal sign-off. Please mark the envelope for sequential signing: Equinox procurement -> Equinox legal -> Redwood legal -> Redwood finance.

We appreciate the capped credit approach and monthly invoicing — that should simplify internal approvals. I'll escalate the termination clause to legal, but the 60-day unwind guard should be OK for our commercial director.

I'll confirm once procurement has routed the redline.

Thanks,
Maria
